newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA to cut fewer Airbus jobs.
newsitem.headline: DASA to cut fewer Airbus jobs.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace Airbus GmbH, the German plane maker in the Airbus consortium, will shed only a fraction of the jobs it had planned to, the Hamburger Abendblatt newspaper said on Friday.
"Planned staff cuts will be heavily reduced," chief executive Gustav Humpert told the paper. The company is a unit of DASA, which itself belongs to auto giant Daimler-Benz AG.
Around 500 of the Hamburg-based company's 14,400 workforce will lose their jobs by the end of the year -- 3,400 fewer than originally planned.
Humpert said that "the steepest increase in production that we have ever had" was responsible for the change in strategy.
Boosted by strong U.S. orders, production of the smaller A319, A320 and A321 Airbus models will rise from 72 last year to 130 this year. Next year, production is set at 173 and 1999 at 207 jets.
